{{Short description|German chemist (born 1940)}}
'''Bernd Giese''' (born 2 June 1940 in Hamburg, Germany) is a German chemist and guest professor in [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Fribourg]] in [[Fribourg]], Switzerland since 2010.<ref name="orchid" />

==Biography==
Born in [[Hamburg]], Germany, Giese received his PhD from [[LMU Munich]] under [[Rolf Huisgen]] in 1969.{{efn|Title of the dissertation: ''Beiträge zum Mechanismus der Amin-Addition an Acetylen-Carbonester'' {{OCLC|62794433}}}} From 1969 to 1971, he worked in pharmaceutical research at [[BASF]] in Ludwigshafen. He obtained his [[Habilitation]] from the [[University of Freiburg]] in 1976. From 1977 to 1988, he was full professor at the [[Technical University of Darmstadt]]<ref name="unibas" /> and from 1989 to 2010 at the [[University of Basel]].<ref name="orchid">{{ORCID|0000-0002-6975-8608}}</ref>

==Research==
Giese specializes in the bio-[[organic chemistry]] and synthesis of radicals in biological systems.<ref>{{cite book | editor-last = Taylor | editor-first = Peter | title = Mechanism and Synthesis | publisher = Royal Society of Chemistry | year = 2002 | isbn = 978-0-85404-695-9 }}</ref><ref name="Thomson" /><ref name="chemie1.unibas.ch 2020">{{cite web | title=research2 | website=chemie1.unibas.ch | date=13 June 2020 | url=https://www.chemie1.unibas.ch/~giese/research.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200613035856/https://www.chemie1.unibas.ch/~giese/research.html | archive-date=13 June 2020 | url-status=unfit | access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref> He contributed to the understanding of radical induced [[DNA]] cleavage and of the DNA synthesis by [[ribonucleotide reductase]].<ref name="AAAS" /> He discovered that long range charge transfer through DNA and Peptides occurs by a hopping mechanism.<ref name="AAAS" /><ref name="Giese2000">{{cite journal|last1=Giese|first1=Bernd|title=Long-Distance Charge Transport in DNA: The Hopping Mechanism|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=33|issue=9|year=2000|pages=631–636|issn=0001-4842|doi=10.1021/ar990040b|pmid=10995201}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meggers|first1=Eric|last2=Michel-Beyerle|first2=Maria E.|last3=Giese|first3=Bernd|date=Dec 1998|title=Sequence Dependent Long Range Hole Transport in DNA|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ja983092p|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|language=en|volume=120|issue=49|pages=12950–12955|doi=10.1021/ja983092p|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The formation of carbon–carbon bonds by addition of free radicals to [[alkene]]s is called the [[Giese reaction]].<ref name="Giese1983">{{cite journal|last1=Giese|first1=Bernd|title=Formation of CC Bonds by Addition of Free Radicals to Alkenes|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|volume=22|issue=10|year=1983|pages=753–764|issn=0570-0833|doi=10.1002/anie.198307531}}</ref> Giese developed concepts, guidelines, and synthetic applications for the stereochemistry of radical reactions.<ref name="CurranPorter1995">{{cite book|last1=Curran|first1=Dennis P.|last2=Porter|first2=Ned A.|last3=Giese|first3=Bernd|title=Stereochemistry of Radical Reactions: Concepts, Guidelines, and Synthetic Applications|year=1995|doi=10.1002/9783527615230|isbn=978-3-527-29372-8}}</ref>

==Awards==
* 1976 Karl-Winnacker Award<ref name="unibas">{{cite web | title=curriculum2 | website=chemie1.unibas.ch | date=13 June 2020 | url=https://www.chemie1.unibas.ch/~giese/curriculum.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200613013740/https://www.chemie1.unibas.ch/~giese/curriculum.html | archive-date=13 June 2020 | url-status=unfit | access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref>
* 1977 {{ill|Carl-Duisberg Award|de|Carl-Duisberg-Gedächtnispreis}}<ref name="unibas" />
* 1987 [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]]<ref name="unibas" />
* 1988 Merck-Schuchardt Award<ref name="unibas" />
* 1999 Member of the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]<ref name="unibas" /><ref name="Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina 2021">{{cite web | title=Mitglieder | website=Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften Leopoldina | date=25 September 2021 | url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/bernd-giese/ | language=de | access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref>
* 2003 Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name="unibas" /><ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |title=Bernd Giese |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/bernd-giese |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref>
* 2005 [[Tetrahedron Prize]] for Creativity in [[Organic Chemistry]] & BioMedicinal Chemistry<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.journals.elsevier.com/tetrahedron/awards/tetrahedron-prize-for-creativity-in-organic-chemistry-2019|title = Tetrahedron Prize for Creativity in Organic Chemistry |publisher = Elsevier|access-date = 28 January 2015 |url-status = live|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140909101444/http://www.elsevier.com/physical-sciences/chemistry/organic-chemistry/tetrahedron-prize-for-creativity-in-organic-chemistry-or-bioorganic-medicinal-chemistry|archive-date = 9 September 2014}}</ref>
* 2006 [[Emil Fischer Medal]] of the Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker<ref name="unibas" />
* 2009 Norris Award in Physical Organic Chemistry of the American Chemical Society<ref name="unibas" />
* 2012 {{ill|Paracelsus Prize|de|Paracelsus-Preis}} of the Swiss Chemical Society<ref name="unibas" />

[[Reuters|Reuters News agency]] predicted him as a possible [[Nobel Laureate]] in Chemistry in 2009.<ref name="Thomson">{{Cite web |url=http://thomsonreuters.com/content/press_room/sci/nobel_prize_predicitions_2009 |title=Thomson Reuters Predicts Nobel Laureates |access-date=19 November 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091008115717/http://thomsonreuters.com/content/press_room/sci/nobel_prize_predicitions_2009 |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 October 2009}}</ref>
